nodes.description: Incorporation of pN-collagen chains into assembling type I collagen fibrils produces fibrils of irregular contour and reduced diameter, with lower fibril density in the dermis than normal. This differs from the flattened "hieroglyphic" ribbon morphology of dermatosparaxis EDS, in which essentially all secreted collagen retains its N-propeptide; here only a fraction of chains are affected, since the unaffected allele continues to produce normally processed chains.

nodes.description: A heterozygous single-base substitution at the consensus GT splice-donor dinucleotide of intron 6, or a nearby splice-disrupting variant, causes exon 6 to be skipped during COL1A2 pre-mRNA splicing, deleting the N-telopeptide-encoding sequence from a fraction of proalpha2(I) chains.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in the pro alpha 2(I) gene (COL1A2) for type I procollagen in Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type VII: evidence suggesting that skipping of exon 6 in RNA splicing may be a common cause of the phenotype.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of genomic clones revealed a single-base mutation that converted the first nucleotide of intron 6 from G to A. Therefore, the mutation was a change, in the -GT-consensus splice site, that produced efficient exon skipping.

nodes.description: Newborns with arthrochalasia EDS show distinctive craniofacial and ectodermal features -- mild hypertelorism, bilateral epicanthal folds, large fontanels, pronounced micrognathia, and sparse hair -- that are consistently reported alongside the joint and skin manifestations. The cited sources document these as recognizable diagnostic clues but do not state a mechanism connecting them to the type I collagen exon-6-skipping defect; this edge is recorded without a mechanistic claim.

nodes.description: Exon 6 encodes 18 amino acids of the N-telopeptide that carry both the procollagen N-proteinase cleavage site and a collagen cross-linking lysine residue. Chains lacking this exon cannot be cleaved by procollagen N-proteinase (ADAMTS2) at their normal site, converging on the same molecular defect that biallelic ADAMTS2 loss causes in dermatosparaxis EDS, but here arising from the substrate rather than the enzyme.
